response: Because the quadratic has exactly one real solution, its discriminant is zero. Write a=k^A, b=k^B, and c=k^C, where the exponents are integers. Then k^(2B)=4k^(A+C), so k^(2B-A-C)=4. The case k=1 is impossible. Since k is a positive integer greater than 1, the only possibilities are k=2 with 2B-A-C=2, or k=4 with 2B-A-C=1. The repeated root is r=b/(2a)=k^(B-A)/2. If k=2, r is an integral power of 2, and the largest such power below 100 is 64. If k=4, the possible values are 4^t/2 for integers t; the largest one below 100 is 4^3/2=32, since 4^4/2=128. Hence r cannot exceed 64. This value is attainable: take k=2, a=2, b=256, and c=8192. These are powers of 2, the discriminant is 256^2-4(2)(8192)=0, and the repeated root is 256/(2·2)=64. Therefore the maximum possible value of r is 64.

For every polynomial f with integer coefficients and all integers u and v, the difference f(u)-f(v) is divisible by u-v. Indeed, for each nonnegative integer j, u^j-v^j is divisible by u-v, and an integer linear combination of such differences has the same property. Applying this with u=2010 and v=2008 shows that 2 must divide f(2010)-f(2008). Under the stated assumptions this difference is 1867-0=1867, which is odd. This contradiction proves that no such polynomial exists.

Let c=f(0). Setting y=0 in the given equation yields f(f(x))=x+ac for every rational x. Consequently f is injective: if f(u)=f(v), applying f to both sides gives u+ac=v+ac. It is also surjective, because any rational t equals f(f(t-ac)). Now fix arbitrary rationals u and y, and choose x with f(x)=u. The original equation gives f(u+ay)=af(y)+x. The identity f(f(x))=x+ac also gives f(u)=x+ac, so x=f(u)-ac. Therefore f(u+ay)=f(u)+af(y)-ac. Since a is nonzero, for arbitrary rational v we may put y=v/a and obtain f(u+v)=f(u)+af(v/a)-ac. Taking u=0 in this identity shows af(v/a)-ac=f(v)-c. Hence f(u+v)=f(u)+f(v)-c for all rationals u,v. Define g(x)=f(x)-c. Then g is additive on the rationals. If q=g(1), additivity gives g(n)=nq for every integer n, and from n·g(m/n)=g(m) it gives g(m/n)=(m/n)q for every rational m/n. Thus f(x)=qx+c for some rational q. Substitution into the original equation gives q^2x+q c+qay+c=x+aqy+ac. The coefficients of x imply q^2=1, while the constant terms imply (q+1-a)c=0; the coefficients of y already agree. Thus q=-1 forces c=0 because a is nonzero, while q=1 permits exactly those c for which (2-a)c=0. Conversely, direct substitution verifies every resulting function. Therefore all solutions are f(x)=-x, and f(x)=x+c where c is rational and (2-a)c=0. Equivalently, f(x)=x is always a solution, and when a=2 every rational translation f(x)=x+c is a solution as well.

For each element t of {1,2,...,2019}, count the n-tuples for which t belongs to A_1 union ... union A_n. There are 2^(2019n) n-tuples in total. If t is absent from every A_i, each A_i can be any subset of the other 2018 elements, giving 2^(2018n) tuples. Thus t belongs to the union in exactly 2^(2019n)-2^(2018n) tuples. The size of a union is the sum, over its 2019 possible elements, of the indicator that the element occurs. Summing these indicators first over tuples and then over elements therefore gives the required value 2019(2^(2019n)-2^(2018n)).

Suppose first that a<b. Since the floor function is nondecreasing, floor(a) is at most floor(b). It follows that a+floor(a)<b+floor(b), contradicting the assumed equality. The alternative b<a gives the same contradiction with a and b interchanged. Neither strict inequality is possible, so a=b.

Set theta_n=pi/4-npi/6. The tangent subtraction identity gives tan(theta-pi/6)=(sqrt(3)tan(theta)-1)/(tan(theta)+sqrt(3)). Since a_0=1=tan(pi/4), induction therefore gives a_n=tan(theta_n). There is no exceptional denominator in this induction: tan(theta_n)=-sqrt(3) would require theta_n to be congruent to -pi/3 modulo pi, which after multiplying the congruence by 12/pi would give 2n congruent to 7 modulo 12, an impossibility. Likewise theta_n is never congruent to pi/2 modulo pi, so all these tangents are defined. Because tangent has period pi and 2017 is congruent to 1 modulo 6, a_2017=tan(pi/4-pi/6)=tan(pi/12). Finally, tan(pi/12)=tan(pi/4-pi/6)=(1-1/sqrt(3))/(1+1/sqrt(3))=2-sqrt(3). Thus a=2, b=-1, and c=3, so a+b+c=4.

We use the standard convention that binomial(n,k)=0 when k>n. First, no value can occur twice in the list: if a_i=a_j with i>j, then binomial(a_i,a_j)=binomial(a_i,a_i)=1, which is not divisible by 17. Since every a_i is one of the 2024 integers 0,1,...,2023, this proves m<=2024. The bound is attained by listing all of them in strictly decreasing order: a_1=2023, a_2=2022, ..., a_2024=0. Whenever i>j, one has a_i<a_j, so binomial(a_i,a_j)=0, which is divisible by 17. Therefore the largest possible value of m is 2024.

Let r_i be the number of marbles in row i and c_j the number in column j. Both sets of ten counts have sum 33. If square (i,j) is empty, the number written there is r_i+c_j; the row and column marbles counted here are disjoint because their only possible intersection is the empty square itself. If r_i+c_j were summed over all 100 squares, the result would be 10 times the sum of the row counts plus 10 times the sum of the column counts, namely 660. On the occupied squares, the total of r_i+c_j is sum_i r_i^2+sum_j c_j^2. Hence the desired sum is S=660-sum_i r_i^2-sum_j c_j^2. For ten nonnegative integer counts with sum 33, the sum of their squares is minimized when no two counts differ by more than 1: if x>=y+2, replacing x,y by x-1,y+1 lowers the square sum by 2(x-y)-2>0. Thus the minimum consists of three counts equal to 4 and seven equal to 3, with square sum 3·16+7·9=111. Applying this separately to rows and columns gives S<=660-111-111=438. It remains to show attainability. Number rows and columns modulo 10. Put marbles in every square (i,j) for which j-i is 0, 1, or 2 modulo 10; this places three marbles in each row and column. Then add marbles at (0,3), (1,4), and (2,5), which were empty. Now exactly three rows and three columns have count 4, and all the others have count 3. Thus equality holds, and the maximum sum is 438.
